title: File watcher that reruns a task on change
when: The user wants a script that rebuilds, copies, tests or reloads automatically whenever files in a folder change.
prompt:
Goal: A watcher that reacts once per burst of changes, ignores noise and never runs two jobs at once.
Steps:
1. If the job is only restarting one script, use node --watch file.mjs and stop there.
2. Otherwise start with #!/usr/bin/env node, take folder and task from process.argv, exit with code 1 when the folder is missing.
3. fs.watch(dir, { recursive: true }, (type, name) => ...); name can be null, so guard it; ignore dot files, ~ .swp .tmp, the output folder, node_modules.
4. Debounce 150 ms, collecting changed paths in a Set, then run the task once with the list.
5. Serialize: while a run is active set pending, and start one more run when it ends; log time, files and duration, catch task errors.
6. Close watchers on SIGINT.
Quality bar:
- One save triggers exactly one run.
- Task errors never kill the watcher.
- Generated files never retrigger it.
Pitfalls:
- Watching the output folder, which loops forever.
- Trusting the event type; editors often save via rename.
- Recursive mode missing on some platforms; fall back to one watcher per folder.
Verify:
- [ ] Debounce timer and a Set of paths.
- [ ] A running flag prevents overlap.
- [ ] Ignore list includes the output folder.
- [ ] SIGINT closes watchers.
Output: scripts/watch.mjs plus a "watch" entry in package.json scripts.

examples.input: rebuild the css every time I save a file in src
examples.output: watch.mjs with fs.watch recursive, 150 ms debounce, no overlapping runs
